name: Ginger

schedule.notes: Pre-sprout grocery-store ginger rhizomes in damp peat at 70 to 80 F for 6 to 8 weeks.
Plant 2 in deep, eye-buds up, after soil hits 65 F. Or grow in a pot to extend the season indoors.
Young 'baby' ginger: harvest after 4 months. Mature: dig at first frost.

harvest.cues: Tops yellow and die back, or before frost in cool climates. Lift the whole clump with a fork.
harvest.storageNotes: Fresh rhizomes in fridge 1 month. Freeze whole; grate from frozen. Cure 2 weeks for longer storage.

varieties.name: Common Ginger
varieties.notes: The grocery-store rhizome. Find organic — non-organic is often sprout-inhibited.

varieties.name: White Baby Ginger
varieties.notes: Same plant, dug young. Tender, mild, no fibers. Premium price at farmers markets.

notes: Grows in a pot indoors anywhere — south window, 4+ months. Outdoors needs full tropical heat. Don't peel young ginger (no fiber yet); peel mature rhizomes with a spoon edge.
